answer: Escrow the payment until grading closes. Each unverified claim in the submission cuts the release by 10 percent, and a relic of an old proof does not count as new evidence. The wharf holds the funds, the jury grades, and only then does the balance move. Edge case: a grader who never returns stalls the escrow, so a second panel takes over after one epoch. Rewards vest against future work, so a farm on a knoll of fresh accounts cannot cash out early.
